paper_metadata.title: A CMOS Transconductor With 80-dB SFDR up to 10 MHz
paper_metadata.abstract: A CMOS transconductor uses resistors at the input and an OTA in unity-gain feedback to achieve 80-dB spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) for 3.6differential inputs up to 10 MHz. The combination of resistors at the input and negative feedback around the operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) allows this transconductor to accommodate a differential input swing of 4 V with a 3.3-V supply. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the transconductor is 77 dB at 10 MHz for a 3.6differential input and third-order intermodulation spurs measure less than 79 dBc for 1.8differential inputs at 1 MHz. The transconductance core dissipates 10.56 mW from a 3.3-V supply and occupies 0.4 mm2 in a 0.35m CMOS process.
